title: Neural Engine
description: A modular deep learning framework built from scratch in NumPy. Features vectorised backpropagation, automatic gradient derivations, and SGD optimizers, achieving ~97.5% accuracy on MNIST without PyTorch or external ML libraries.
question: How does Backpropagation work? What is the Hebbian Theory?
journey: I wanted to see if I could build a working neural network library using just NumPy. Instead of using automatic differentiation, I derived the matrix calculus for the forward and backward passes on paper first.
The library is modular (similar to PyTorch) and includes dense layers, He initialization, ReLU activations, SGD, and a fused Softmax + Cross-Entropy loss layer that prevents overflow errors.
I trained it on MNIST using mini-batching and hit ~97.5% test accuracy. It was a great project to understand loss gradients, matrix multiplication, and training mechanics at a low level.

title: Early Projects (2020-2022)
description: Archived GitHub containing my earliest learning from middle school. No longer maintained since 4+ years.
question: Why is this so fun, and what more can I do?
journey: When I first started programming around ages 11-13, learning was just trial and error, writing small scripts to see what worked on screen.

This old account holds that initial learning phase: Early Websites, AI Experimentation, Arduino, Image Processing, Etc. Although I never fully understood the math going on behind the scenes when experimenting with these tools, I genuinely liked to tinker with them, this phase helps me appreciate today the value of building things from scratch and understanding the insane amount of math and effort that goes behind the things we take for granted.
While long retired and unmaintained, I keep this account around as a nostalgic reminder of how I first got started with programming.
Consider this a wild software museum piece, unmaintained and untouched.
